leftEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
leftEvidence.title: The wilderness generation becomes a present warning about rest

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The psalm addresses present hearers: “Today, if you will hear his voice,” and warns against hardening hearts as at Meribah and Massah.
points.right: Hebrews quotes the psalm’s “today,” warns against an unbelieving heart, and asks who rebelled after hearing.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Forty years of grief ends with an oath that the generation will not enter the LORD’s rest.
points.right: Those who sinned fell in the wilderness, and the conclusion names unbelief as the reason they could not enter.

payload.posture: Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 and applies its voice, hardening, wilderness death, and rest warning to a present community.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: Hebrews asks who rebelled and why they could not enter

payload.tension: The later argument identifies unbelief while preserving the psalm’s direct appeal to hear today.
payload.title: “Today” and the warning against unbelief
